nodes.title: Distinguish failure from EOF in cram_cat()
nodes.body:
`cram_read_container()` returns `NULL` for both EOF and errors, so it's necessary to call `cram_eof()` to tell them apart.

Also adds checks for errors from `cram_filter_container()` and `cram_transcode_rg()` so failures in these functions do not go unnoticed. (Note that while `cram_filter_container()` is [documented](https://github.com/samtools/htslib/blob/054ba580ae95178a2092225ea04a659d933ce41c/htslib/cram.h#L341) as returning -1 on EOF and -2 for errors, it looks like it will actually [return -1 for various error conditions](https://github.com/samtools/htslib/blob/054ba580ae95178a2092225ea04a659d933ce41c/cram/cram_external.c#L882).  This shouldn't be a problem as we don't expect to see EOFs at the point where `cram_filter_container()` is called, and if there is one it was probably a truncated file.)


Fixes #2401

nodes.title: markdup `-d`: incorrect optical calls across tiles with mixed prefix lengths
nodes.body:
I found a bug in function `check_duplicate_chain`
(bam_markdup.c#L1285-L1401 in 75c906ac) in which the grouping of name
prefixes in the optical check ends only on an equal-length, different
prefix in read-encoded flow cell information. The result is erroneous
marking of reads on different tiles as optical duplicates (as they’re
compared by x/y only).

The bug is triggered by (1) flow cell tile numbers with different
digit counts and (2) names that can’t be parsed, leaving fields unset.
(It’s something I tested out of caution and is probably unexpected in
data unless sequencing runs were merged and/or reads renamed.)

This fix (1) ends a group when the prefix lengths differ; (2) marks
unparsed names as -1, preventing their comparison (as a valid parse
with no tile part has length 0, hence -1); and (3) calls `memcmp` on
only positive lengths.

I’ve added a new test 22 with three sets: (1) unparsed name, (2) mixed
tile lengths, and (3) same-tile control.

Fixes #2399.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-opus-5-5
Signed-off-by: Kris Alavattam <34422552+kalavattam@users.noreply.github.com>

nodes.title: Make samtools import accept empty FASTQ input
nodes.body:
In the rare, but occasional situation where a sequencing library failed or yielded no reads, I'd like to make samtools and other tools more graceful in consuming that data instead of aborting and causing my pipeline to crash.

When `samtools import` is given empty inputs, it aborrts with "truncated file. Aborting" and exit status 1. This happens if the input is a file or on stdin and in every input mode (`-s`, `-0`, `-1`/`-2`, `--i1`/`--i2`, positional).

I think an empty FASTQ is a legitimate input (e.g. upstream step that filters reads,  empty sequencing run, etc.).

And, for comparison and justification sake, `samtools fastq` itself writes an empty output for a header-only file.

This exception happens because HTSlib detects zero-length input as `empty_format`, and `sam_read1()` deliberately returns `-3`, so a failing command piped into `samtools view` is reported as an error.

With this PR, the subcommand `import` now treats this case as end of file once `hts_getline()` confirms the stream is empty, and writes a header-only file with the same `@HD`, `@CO`, `@RG` and `@PG` lines that the non-empty case gets. The extra check matters because a gzip file truncated before its first decompressed byte is also detected as `empty_format`; it still fails as before. Tests cover an empty `-s` file and stdin, empty `-1`/`-2` files, `-r`/`-R` read groups in the empty output's header, and a truncated gzip that must still fail.

nodes.title: stats: count duplicates for the same records as "sequences"; include isize 0 in the SD
nodes.body:
Fixes #696.

Two small corrections to `samtools stats` SN numbers, one commit each, both in `stats.c`,
each with a regression test that fails on `develop`.

**Duplicate counts** (99c2244). `reads duplicated` and `bases duplicated` were accumulated
before the `IS_ORIGINAL()` gate in `collect_stats()`, so secondary and supplementary
records carrying the 0x400 flag were counted, while `sequences` and `total length` exclude
those records. A duplication rate formed from the two lines (MultiQC's samtools stats
module does this) was overstated once the supplementary records of duplicates were
flagged, which is what `samtools markdup -S` and Picard MarkDuplicates produce. This is
the move suggested in #696: the counting now happens inside the `IS_ORIGINAL()` block,
next to the read length counts, so the two pairs of lines refer to the same records. On
`test/stat/22_dup_supp.sam` (20 reads, 8 duplicates, 4 supplementary records belonging to
duplicate pairs) `develop` reports `reads duplicated: 10` and `bases duplicated: 860`
against `sequences: 20`; this branch reports 8 and 800. `flagstat` already distinguishes
`duplicates` from `primary duplicates`; `stats` had no such pair.

**Insert size standard deviation** (723af0e). The SD loop in `output_stats()` started at
`isize = 1`, while the mean and the count over the same bins started at 0, so pairs
reported with TLEN 0 entered the denominator but not the sum of squares and lowered the
SD instead of raising it. The loop now starts at 0, like the two loops before it. On
`test/stat/23_isize_zero.sam` (10 pairs, two with TLEN 0, the rest 300 to 360) `develop`
reports an SD of 60.1 against a mean of 259.0; the correct value for that mean is 130.5.
Whether the isize 0 bin belongs in these statistics at all is a separate question; this
change only makes the SD consistent with the mean printed next to it. Happy to drop this
commit if you would rather take it separately.

Tests: two new `test_cmd` entries in `test/test.pl` compare the SN lines named above; both
fail on unmodified `develop` (de749a6) and pass with this branch. `perl test/test.pl`:
1011 passed, 0 failed, 32 expected failures; `make test` passes. NEWS entries included
under "Bug fixes".

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5-1

Found in Mytochondria, a volunteer project that checks the numerical core of research software and verifies every finding by execution (methods and harnesses: https://github.com/cindykrafft/mytochondria/tree/main/audits/samtools)

nodes.title: stats: grow the coverage ring buffer instead of wrapping around
nodes.body:
Fixes #2378.

`samtools stats` accumulates the coverage distribution (`COV` rows and the `-t`/`-g`
target percentage) in a ring buffer of `5 × nbases` cells indexed modulo its size
relative to the current read start. An aligned block ending more than that beyond the
read start — the far exon of a spliced alignment — wrapped around onto positions near
the read start. With 100-bp reads any intron longer than about 1.4 kb triggers it; on a
simulated six-exon gene the covered-position count was 18 % too high and the `-t`/`-g`
percentage was reported as 117.77 %.

This makes `round_buffer_insert_read()` grow the buffer (doubling, linearising the
pending counts) whenever a block would reach beyond it, through a new
`round_buffer_resize()`. The same helper replaces the copy in `realloc_buffers()`, which
passed element counts to `memcpy()` where byte counts were needed and dropped three
quarters of the pending counts whenever a longer read arrived while coverage was pending
near the end of the ring (mixed-length or long-read input).

Memory: the buffer now grows to the longest span between a read start and the end of
one of its blocks, so a 1-Mb intron costs 4 MB of `int`s; previously the size was fixed
at `5 × nbases`. A cap with a warning could be added if that is a concern.

Tests: `test/stat/20_spliced.sam` (the two-read wrap case) and
`test/stat/21_mixed_lengths.sam` (the reallocation case), compared on their `COV` rows;
both fail on unmodified `develop` and pass with this change. `make test` otherwise
unchanged (numbers in the audit's `upstream/README.md`).

NEWS entry included under "Bug fixes".

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-fable-5-1

nodes.title: Check string aux tag types before accessing data
nodes.body:
Following 681b50ea, add more checks on aux tag types to ensure that the stored data is a NUL-terminated string before accessing it.

In most cases tags with unexpected types are simply ignored as if they don't exist.  An exception is samtools stats, which already reports an error if the tag it expects to split on is not present, so now it also does if the tag has the wrong type. The stats code is also made more efficient so that it doesn't try to `strdup()` the tag value unless it needs to add a new hash entry.

The stats man page is updated to note that the tag used for the `-S` option must have a string type.

nodes.title: Move checksum version to 2.0
nodes.body:
Checksum calculations differed between samtools v1.24 and previous
releases.  In earlier releases, the "--check-mate" option produced incorrect
checksums.  This was fixed in v1.24 but made already existing checksums
invalid.

Therefore, the fixed checksum is now designated Checksum 2.0 while the
previous one is left at Checksum 1.0 in order differentiate the versions.

A new "--version-1" option will set samtools checksum to version 1.0
behaviour for backwards compatibility.

Should fix https://github.com/samtools/samtools/issues/2354.

nodes.title: Fix reuse-after-free in bam_plcmd ref cache
nodes.body:
The ref cache tracked 3 references: current, last, and next. It has an implicit assumption that we're never going to be querying more than 3 so it has room for exactly 3 slots.  However some scenarios, both in bam_mplp_auto/next and in the mpileup function logic, causes skipping ahead of multiple references and invalidating the current or last reference.

We still keep to 3 slots, but we make fewer assumptions of ref always being valid and call mplp_get_ref more frequently.  To ensure this isn't a CPU burden it now explicitly tracks current reference id (curr_tid) and ensures that's always slot 0 so the most common case is never expunged and re-fetched too often.

Fixes #2363

nodes.title: Make samtools view --unmap and --unoutput work together
nodes.body:
Unmap turns data that does not pass the filtered into unmapped data, but also changes it to go the normal output stream.

Unoutput redirects data that doesn't pass the filter to go to its own file.

As previously rewitten, unoutput didn't do what it was advertised to do and instead operated on records-not-written rather than records-filtered, so the combination (if permitted) would result in an empty file.  It now does the logical thing, and as advertised in the usage statement based on filtering rather than whether appearing in the output stream.

Fixes #2356

nodes.title: Add shared helper for samtools @PG lines; fix reset/rmdup provenance
nodes.body:
## Summary

Consolidates the duplicated `@PG`-adding code into one shared helper and fixes two subcommands whose `@PG` records were incomplete or missing.

## What changed

**Shared helper.** Every subcommand that writes an alignment file called `sam_hdr_add_pg()` directly with a near-identical block. Those copies are replaced by `samtools_add_pg_line()` (declared in `samtools.h`, implemented in `sam_opts.c`, which is already linked into every subcommand and into `libst.a`). It also folds in the `--no-PG` check, so callers pass their opt-out flag through instead of repeating the condition.

**HTSlib version in `VN`.** When the HTSlib version cannot be deduced from the SAMtools version it is appended to `VN`, e.g. `VN:1.24.1 (with HTSlib 1.25)`. Since the two are released together with matching major and minor version numbers, **`VN` is unchanged in the usual case** and no expected test outputs move.

**Provenance fixes.**
- `reset` wrote a `@PG` line with a command line but no `VN`, unlike every other subcommand. Fixed.
- `rmdup`/`rmdupse` wrote no `@PG` line at all. They now add one and accept `--no-PG`.

**Consistency.** `ampliconclip`'s inverted `add_pg` flag is renamed to the `no_pg` convention used everywhere else.

## Testing

- `make test` — 1000 passed, 0 failures.
- `make maintainer-check` — PASS.
- `test/test.pl` is untouched: because `VN` is unchanged when the versions match, no harness change or expected-output regeneration is needed.
- The version-mismatch branch cannot be exercised through the CLI (`hts_version()` is fixed at link time), so its logic was verified separately across matching, patch-differing (`1.23.1`/`1.23.2`), major/minor-differing, and unparseable-version cases.

## Changes from the first revision

Addresses @daviesrob's review:
- HTSlib version moved from a `DS` field to being appended to `VN`, and omitted when it can be deduced from the SAMtools version.
- Dropped `REPRODUCIBILITY.md`, the `README.md` change, and the sort thread-comparison test.

nodes.title: Fill in mate information on supplementary alignments in fixmate
nodes.body:
`samtools sort --template-coordinate` requires an `MC` tag on every paired, mate-mapped read, but `samtools fixmate` sets `MC` (and the other mate information) only on primary alignments. Supplementary alignments — emitted for split reads by e.g. `bwa mem` — reach the sorter without `MC`, so it aborts:

```
[bam_sort] error: no MC tag. Please run samtools fixmate on file first.
```

fixmate now fills in mate information (coordinates, orientation, `MC` and `MQ`) on supplementary alignments too, taken from the mate's primary and reusing the helpers already applied to the primary pair. Secondary alignments are left unchanged, matching Picard/htsjdk and fgbio: a supplementary shares its read's primary mate, whereas a secondary is an alternative mapping with no well-defined mate.

The change only adds mate information that was previously absent on supplementary records, so existing output is unaffected and the test suite passes unchanged. Adds a `fixmate` fixture and an end-to-end `sort --template-coordinate` test covering a supplementary alignment.

nodes.title: Change nquals from 256 to 257 for samtools stats.
nodes.body:
The maximum quality in ASCII is 94 (127-33) so anything else is outside of the legal range.  However even if we wanted to handle illegal BAM and ignore the unprintable nature of SAM, using 256 is a bad choice.

The reason is down to how CPU caches work.  They're typically an N-way associative hash when each hash bucket can cache results for N addresses and the hash index is just the last bits of the memory address.  This means a power of 2 in the memory address will put a lot pile many addresses into the same bucket, saturating "N".

A trivial workaround is to multiply by 257 instead of 256, causing the bottom bits of the address to not repeatedly collide.  95 is a better multiplier however as it uses less memory and hence with it further reduces cache miss rates.

Benchmarks from perf stat:

nquals=256:

         267540049      cache-misses              #   11.334 % of all cache refs
        2360568687      cache-references

      20.572468682 seconds time elapsed

nquals=257:

          78089279      cache-misses              #    3.391 % of all cache refs
        2302704223      cache-references

      15.710843218 seconds time elapsed

nquals=95:

          45394053      cache-misses              #    2.102 % of all cache refs
        2159597370      cache-references

      13.713247565 seconds time elapsed

Quite a good speed up for such a tiny change.
*However* setting nquals=95 isn't sufficient as qual "*" is an array of 255 values in BAM (sigh).  So it needs to be >= 256.  We could fix this by mapping 255 to 95 say or better still using a generic mapping table based on real data which would vastly reduce memory for NovaSeq, but this needs buffering and multi-pass, or the ability to add new entries to the lookup table and shuffle around existing entries.  Hence this PR is the trivial win only.

The actual code in CPU cycles for the original was:

```
  0.12 │       addsd    0x218(%r15),%xmm0                                                                        
       │     quals[ i*stats->nquals+qual ]++;                                                                    
  0.22 │       addq     $0x1,(%rdx,%r8,8)                                                                        
       │     stats->sum_qual += qual;                                                                            
 52.52 │       movsd    %xmm0,0x218(%r15)                                                                        
       │     for (i=0; i<seq_len; i++)                                                                           
```

With nquals=95 the change it is:

```
(as above)
 35.44 │       movsd    %xmm0,0x218(%r15)
```

(perf stats -n showed 37176 counts to 18470 counts).  I didn't record it for nquals=257 as I didn't notice the qual "*" issue until later, however the elapsed time is the key indicator.

nodes.title: Ensure indirect function calls have the correct type.
nodes.body: Use new HTSlib interfaces khgetline() and kfgetline() in place of kgetline().  Fixes complaints about undefined behaviour from clang's UBsan due to function pointers passed to kgetline() having the wrong type for the last parameter (it wants a void *, but was given functions taking either FILE * or hFILE *). The new interfaces wrap the calls to kgetline() so there is no need to pass a function pointer.

nodes.title: Fix for the footgun of repeated use of "samtools view --subsample" with the same (or default) seed
nodes.body:
Changes the default seed from 0, to a value derived from the hash of the incoming file's header. The idea is that the default seed should be deterministic given the same input, but different for different inputs.  This ensures the seed is the same regardless of format (SAM/BAM/CRAM) or compression level, but will generally cause the seed to vary for files that have been processed differently due to the differing @PG lines (and possibly others) in the header.  Since "samtools view" will insert a @PG line into the header, serial downsampling of file A to file B to file C will now use different seeds at each step.

I think this is my first PR in samtools, and this changes the a command line default, so I am mindful that this may not be accepted, or not accepted without changes.  I'm very open to feedback here, but would love to fix this footgun, and this seems like a reasonable way to do it.

Fixes #1201, which is something I also run into once in a while when I forget about the default behavior.

In main_cram_size(), close the input hFILE if it fails to covert to a samFile.

nodes.title: Limit sort memory in "samtools split" test
nodes.body: The default sort buffer size is much bigger than necessary for the tests, and can lead to spurious failures on constrained test environments.  Add the same option used elsewhere to ensure sort processes don't run out of memory.

nodes.title: Fix grep for OpenBSD
nodes.body: In OpenBSD, grep needs to have the input file after the options.  This was causing fails in the testing.

nodes.title: Wrap ctype.h functions to avoid array subscript warnings
nodes.body:
Copy HTSlib's internal wrappers for interfaces in `<ctype.h>` into `sam_utils.h` (as it's widely included already) and use them on cases where the input has `char` type.  Fixes "array subscript has type 'char'" warnings on platforms that still implement them as a macro around an array look-up.

The ctype interface wrappers were originally authored by John Marshall in HTSlib commit [fc9aeb6f7](https://github.com/samtools/htslib/commit/fc9aeb6f7).

nodes.title: Fix ubsan warning in threaded consensus pileup mode
nodes.body: A block of data that's entirely empty would attempt to write an empty kstring.

nodes.title: mpileup changes to use kstring for speed up
nodes.body:
Changed direct file writes to kstring buffer and wrote it at end of processing for each line (main contributor in improvement).
Updated reference data retrieval function invoke to execute only on tid change (not a big contributor but gets invoked on every read).
Also there is an htslib update, to prefetch next data to use.

This showed 10 - 30% improvement with different test data.

Attempts to improve #2293

nodes.title: reference file support for reset
nodes.body:
Fixes #2297 
Enabled the reference, input format and output format options for reset.
Reference file can be passed using either -T or --reference options and cram with external reference should work fine.
Input and output format options enabled to use customisation on input and output files.

nodes.title: Add a --regions-file BED-FILE option to samtools consensus
nodes.body:
Note this also changes the output format slightly so include ">chr:start-end" instead of just ">chr".  This makes it comparable to faidx and helps identify separate regions.

Fixes #2288

Some sub-commands such as view distinguish between --regions-file BED which uses indices to do random access and -L BED which uses streaming and filtering instead.  I implemented the former only.

nodes.title: Input validation on some numeric command-line values
nodes.body:
Sanity-check some numeric values passed on the command-line, and error out on malformed strings. 

Motivating example: Raise an error on the bogus command-line `samtools sort -@ -n input.bam -O bam -o sorted.bam` which is missing a thread count after -@. (The current behavior is to set thread count to 0 and drop the `-n` flag, since `atoi("-n")` simply returns zero)

There's more that could be done to validate inputs, but this adds some safety railings to prevent unpleasant surprises.

nodes.title: Fix variable expansion error in seq_cache_populate.py
nodes.body: In an effort to mimick `seq_cache_populate.pl` the output messages are kept the same as much as possible. Unfortunately I missed a perl variable expansion back then.

nodes.title: Add seq_cache_populate.py to MISC_SCRIPTS for installation
nodes.body: The faster python script contributed by @rhpvorderman in #2231 is currently available only in the source tree. It should be installed to `{prefix}/bin/` along with the other scripts so that it can be used with common installation like `brew install samtools`.

nodes.title: Use canonical calloc arguments order for parsed_opts_t allocation
nodes.body:
This commit should NOT produce any change in behavior; swapping the order of the arguments to `calloc()` does NOT affect the behavior of `calloc()`. Thus, the main purpose of this commit is to improve code readability and conformity.

---------

Background: The [C standard](https://en.cppreference.com/w/c/memory/calloc.html) defines the prototype as `calloc(size_t num, size_t size)`. Importantly, "If allocation succeeds, returns a pointer to the lowest (first) byte in the allocated memory block that is suitably aligned for any object type with fundamental alignment."

As `calloc()` only sees the quantity and size of the objects to allocate memory (but NOT the type of the data itself), alignment is not directly dependent on the `size` or `num` argument.

nodes.title: Ignore hard clips in template coordinate sort
nodes.body:
Hard clipping may be variable for reads from the same biochemical template, causing them to sort to different positions. Only soft clips are now considered when calculating unclipped coordinates for template coordinate sorting, matching fgbio behavior.

See: https://github.com/fulcrumgenomics/fgbio/pull/1065

The unclipped_start/end functions now take an include_hard_clips parameter. Template coordinate sort passes 0 (soft clips only), while markdup passes 1 to preserve existing behavior.

Adds test for hard clip handling in template coordinate sort.

nodes.title: Update to split sorted data sequentially and avoid simultaneous open files
nodes.body:
Fixes #2276 
Updated sort to set sub-sort order when sorted with tags. This will set the SO as unsorted and SS as unsorted:<tag>:<secondary sort>.

On split, if the data is sorted by the tag with which it is being split, split is made sequentially instead of opening output files in parallel. If data is not sorted by the split key, split is made by opening output files in parallel as existed.

nodes.title: Add missing sam_global_args_free calls.
nodes.body: These are a memory leak if we use e.g. --input-fmt-options decode_md. Some tools still leak if they get errors and return early, but this is true in many other ways too (for example calmd doesn't destroy the thread pool if it gets an error closing fpout; one among many). However I focused on removing memory leaks on successful execution (albeit harmless due to immediately exiting anyway) as it's more likely to trip up testing.

nodes.title: updated to make consensus work with sam.gz along with threads and ite…
nodes.body:
Consensus crashes when sam.gz is used as input along with threads and iterators.
This happens due to the data validation attempt in sam_parse1 where fp->bam_header, which is null, is used for header.
To avoid this, each fp in thread data is set with a copy of already read header.
This is made for bam and cram as well, for filters to work fine where an expression needs to access the header (like rname, mrname, library etc.)
